# Module overview {#sec-m2}

::: {.modulo-meta}
**Workload:** 6 hours (3h synchronous + 3h asynchronous)\
**Dates:** 05/10 and 06/10 (synchronous); 07/10 (asynchronous)\
**Packages:** `sf`, `terra`, `tidyterra`, `geobr`, `censobr`, `sidrar`, `osmdata`, `elevatr`, `leaflet`, `mapview`, `ggspatial`\
**Case study:** population catchment of the BR-116 highway in the Serra do Mar (PR/SC)
:::

## What you will be able to do by the end of the module

- Read, write and convert spatial data in the formats that circulate in the Ministry:
  `.shp`, `.gpkg`, `.geojson`, `.csv` with coordinates and GeoTIFF.
- Recognise and change coordinate systems without corrupting the geometry, and know **when**
  reprojecting is mandatory.
- Do the operations you now do through menus in QGIS/ArcGIS (*buffer*, intersection,
  clipping, spatial join, area and distance calculations) in code that can be run again.
- Read and process rasters (elevation, land use) and extract values by geometry.
- Download Brazilian public datasets straight from R: IBGE boundaries, Census, SIDRA and
  OpenStreetMap.
- Produce a publication-quality static map and an interactive map for checking.

## Outline

### Synchronous class (3h)

| Block | Content | Chapter |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | The `sf` object: structure, reading, writing, geometry types | @sec-m2-sf |

| 3 | Rasters with `terra`: reading, cropping, map algebra, extraction by geometry | @sec-m2-raster |
| 4 | Geovisualisation: `geom_sf`, `leaflet`, `mapview`, maps for checking | @sec-m2-mapas |

### Asynchronous content (3h)

## Module packages

The simplest way to get everything ready is to run the module's setup script. Open the
course project in RStudio and paste into the console:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joaobazzo/curso-r-transportes/main/R/preparar_modulo2.R")
```
:::


It installs the missing packages, downloads the module data to the project's `dados/` folder and
ends with the message **Tudo pronto para o Módulo 2** ("All set for Module 2"). You can run it more than once: whatever is already
installed or downloaded is skipped.

If you prefer to install by hand, the list below has only what is **new** in this module. `dplyr`,
`ggplot2` and the other Module 1 packages are still in use, with nothing to reinstall.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pacotes <- c("sf", "terra", "tidyterra", "geobr", "censobr", "sidrar",
             "osmdata", "osmextract", "elevatr", "leaflet", "mapview", "ggspatial", "units")

faltando <- setdiff(pacotes, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(faltando) > 0) install.packages(faltando)
```
:::


::: {.callout-important}
## On Windows, install Rtools first

`sf` and `terra` depend on the GDAL, PROJ and GEOS libraries, which are compiled during installation.
Without **Rtools** (see @sec-m1-ambiente) installation fails with a compilation error. Check
afterwards with:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(sf);    sf::sf_extSoftVersion()
library(terra); terra::gdal()
```
:::

:::

## About the *downloads* in this module

The blocks in this module download public data on the first run and **store it on disk**, in
`dados/brutos/`. On later runs, they read from this cache. Rendering is fast and works without
an internet connection. The pattern used throughout the material is this:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
arquivo <- "dados/brutos/municipios_pr.gpkg"

if (!file.exists(arquivo)) {
  muni <- geobr::read_municipality(code_muni = "PR", year = 2022)
  sf::st_write(muni, arquivo, quiet = TRUE)
}
muni <- sf::st_read(arquivo, quiet = TRUE)
```
:::


It is worth adopting this habit in your own scripts: besides speeding things up, it ensures the
analysis keeps reproducing the **same** result when the source dataset is updated.
